app.name: Twalk Companion
app.tagline: The command center for your sovereign messaging hub
screen1.description: Twalk brings all your conversations — WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, Discord, Google Messages — into one place you own, watched over by agents you configure. This Companion sets everything up for you.
screen1.domain.label: Your Twalk domain
screen1.domain.invalid: Please enter a valid domain like {example}.
onboarding.title: Create your account
onboarding.domain: Twalk will set up your account on {domain}.
onboarding.pending.title: This step is on its way
onboarding.pending.body: Account creation and your recovery key arrive with the bootstrap journey. The foundation this screen sits on — the app shell, the Gateway client, the capability check — is in place.
gate.title: This browser cannot run Twalk yet
gate.intro: {count, plural, one {One thing this browser needs is missing.} other {# things this browser needs are missing.}} Twalk does its cryptography here, in the page, so your recovery key never leaves your device — and that needs all of them.
gate.degraded.intro: Everything onboarding needs is here. These extras are not, so some conveniences will be missing.
gate.cause.insecure-context: The page was not loaded over a secure connection. Browsers switch off the cryptography, storage and installation Twalk needs outside HTTPS. Open the Companion over {https}, or over {localhost} while developing.
gate.cause.lockdown-mode: This looks like iOS Lockdown Mode: WebAssembly still runs, but local storage, installation and tab locking are switched off. Open Settings, then Privacy & Security, then Lockdown Mode, and allow this site — or open Twalk in another browser.
gate.cause.storage-blocked: Local storage is switched off. A private window, or a browser setting that blocks site data, does this. Open the Companion in a normal window and allow site data for {origin}.
gate.cause.unsupported-browser: This browser is missing something Twalk needs. Twalk supports Safari on iOS 16.4 and later, and current versions of Chrome, Edge and Firefox.
gate.capability.secure-context.why: HTTPS, or localhost. Everything below depends on it.
gate.capability.webassembly.why: Runs the Matrix cryptography that generates your keys.
gate.capability.storage.why: Keeps your keys on this device, and nowhere else.
gate.capability.crypto-subtle.why: Generates the randomness your recovery key is made of.
gate.capability.service-worker.why: Lets you install Twalk to your home screen.
gate.capability.tab-lock.why: Stops two open tabs from corrupting your keys.
gate.checking: Checking what this browser can do…

qr.whatsapp.title: Connect WhatsApp
qr.whatsapp.caption: Twalk signs in to WhatsApp as one more WhatsApp Web session. Your conversations stay end-to-end encrypted between WhatsApp and Twalk; Twalk only observes them.
qr.whatsapp.disclosure.title: About WhatsApp accounts
qr.whatsapp.disclosure.body: Twalk connects to WhatsApp through the same Web protocol as WhatsApp Web. It works with your personal (free) account and needs no WhatsApp Business account. WhatsApp does not officially support third-party clients: in rare cases, an account using Twalk may be temporarily suspended or banned by WhatsApp. Twalk keeps that risk low by following the Web protocol as strictly as it can, but the risk is not zero. You can dismiss this notice once and it will not come back on this device.
qr.whatsapp.step2: Go to Settings, then Linked devices, then Link a device.
qr.whatsapp.step3: Scan this code with your phone's camera.
qr.whatsapp.alt: Scan this code from WhatsApp, under Settings then Linked devices.
qr.whatsapp.success: WhatsApp is connected. Twalk is now observing your WhatsApp conversations.
qr.whatsapp.trouble1: Your phone has to come online at least once every 12 days for the link to stay active.
qr.whatsapp.trouble2: WhatsApp allows up to 4 linked devices on one account. Remove one in WhatsApp if the code is refused.
qr.whatsapp.trouble3: If the code does not scan, hold the phone steady about 20 cm from the screen, and raise your screen's brightness.
qr.signal.title: Connect Signal
qr.signal.caption: Twalk becomes a linked Signal device on your account, just like Signal Desktop. Your phone stays the primary device and is still what recovers your account.
qr.signal.step2: Go to Settings, then Linked devices.
qr.signal.step3: Tap the plus button (Android) or Link new device (iOS).
qr.signal.note: Signal officially supports linked devices: there is no ban risk. Messages sent before this pairing are not synchronised — Twalk sees new messages only.
qr.signal.alt: Scan this code from Signal, under Settings then Linked devices.
qr.signal.success: Signal is connected. Twalk is now observing your new Signal messages.
qr.signal.trouble1: Your phone must stay online for Signal messages to reach Twalk.
qr.signal.trouble2: If the code is refused, check that Signal on your phone is up to date, then show a new code.
matrix.title: Connect your Matrix account
matrix.caption: If you already use Matrix, Twalk can watch over the account you have rather than create a new one. Twalk invites its Sensor into the rooms you choose, and changes nothing about your other Matrix sessions.
matrix.noFlow: This homeserver offers no sign-in method the Companion can drive. Sign in from your usual Matrix client, then come back.
matrix.qrLater: Signing in by QR code from another Matrix client (MSC4108) arrives with a later version: it carries your encryption secrets across, and that needs machinery these screens deliberately do not load.
matrix.error.unreachable: That homeserver could not be reached. Check the address and your internet connection.
matrix.error.rejected: The homeserver refused those credentials. Check your username and password.
matrix.error.rateLimited: The homeserver is rate-limiting sign-in attempts. Wait a moment, then try again.
matrix.error.refused: The homeserver refused the sign-in. Try again, and open the diagnostics if it persists.
matrix.error.invite: Your Twalk server could not invite the Sensor. Your Matrix session may have expired — sign in again, then retry.
matrix.rooms.intro: These are the rooms {user} has joined. Twalk only learns the ones you tick: the list itself stays in this browser.
matrix.rooms.loading: Reading your rooms from your homeserver…
matrix.rooms.none: This account has joined no rooms yet. Join one from your usual Matrix client, then come back.

matrix.rooms.byMembers: no name: shown by its members, whose display names need machinery these screens do not load

matrix.rooms.onlySelected: Your Matrix password and access token stay in this browser. The only thing sent to your Twalk server is the list of rooms you ticked, and a one-time token that lets it send the invitations.

matrix.done.body: The Sensor joins on its own and starts observing these rooms. Nothing you did not tick is visible to it.
matrix.done.failed: could not be invited — you may not have permission to invite in this room
sms.title: Connect SMS via Google Messages
sms.disclosure.title: This SMS path is a preview
sms.disclosure.body: This is a v0.1 proof of concept. It runs on Google Messages Web, which means your SMS transit through Google's infrastructure and a Google account is required. In v0.2, Twalk replaces it with a first-party Android app that reads SMS straight from your phone with nobody in the middle, and your setup migrates automatically when that ships.
sms.requirement: Twalk uses the Google Messages app on your Android phone to send and receive SMS. You need Google Messages installed and set as the default messaging app on that phone. An iPhone alone cannot use this preview.
sms.ios.title: This preview needs an Android phone
sms.ios.body: SMS through Twalk in v0.1 reads your messages from Google Messages on an Android phone, which iOS does not have. If you own both an iPhone and an Android phone, you can use the Android one as your SMS source. The sovereign path arriving in v0.2 will still need an Android phone.
sms.step1.title: Step 1 — turn on device pairing on your phone
sms.step1.a: Open Google Messages on your Android phone.
sms.step1.b: Tap your profile picture, then Device pairing.
sms.step1.c: Leave that screen open: your phone has to be reachable for the rest of this.
sms.step2.title: Step 2 — hand over your Google Messages session
sms.step2.why: Google switched off the QR sign-in for other Google Messages clients in 2024, so the only way left is to hand over the session cookies your own browser gets when you sign in to Google Messages Web. Twalk cannot read them for you: no web page is allowed to read another site's cookies, and that rule is what protects your other accounts. So you copy them, once.
sms.step2.requirements: Two things to set up first, or the cookies you copy will not work
sms.step2.privateWindow: Use a private window. Signing out of Google in a normal window invalidates the session Twalk is holding, and one day you will sign out without thinking about it. In a private window, close the window instead of signing out and the session stays alive.
sms.step2.dbsc: In Chrome, turn off Device Bound Session Credentials (chrome://flags, search for “device bound”). It ties a Google session to this device's hardware key on purpose, so a copied cookie works nowhere else — including on your Twalk server. It is on by default in recent versions.
sms.step2.a: In a private window, sign in to
sms.step2.b: Pair that browser with your phone by scanning the code Google shows, so the session is a working one.
sms.step2.c: Open the developer tools, go to Application then Cookies, and copy the cookies listed below — or paste the whole Cookie header from the Network tab.
sms.cookies.wanted: {count, plural, one {The cookie your bridge asked for} other {The # cookies your bridge asked for}}:
sms.cookies.whatTheyAre: Together, these are your Google sign-in session: anything holding them can act as you on Google Messages Web for as long as they last. Google documents no lifetime for them, so Twalk promises none — expect to do this again one day. They go to your own Twalk server, which passes them to the bridge and keeps no copy; this browser writes them nowhere. You can end them at any time from your Google account's security settings.
sms.cookies.label: Paste the cookies here
sms.cookies.submit: Send them to my Twalk server
sms.cookies.neverStored: Nothing on this screen is saved in your browser. Close the tab and the paste is gone.
sms.cookies.unreadable: That could not be read as cookies. Paste either “name=value; name=value”, or the JSON your cookie extension exports.
sms.cookies.missing: These are missing: {names}. Check you copied every row, including the ones your browser hides behind a scroll.
sms.emoji.body: Your phone is showing an emoji. Check that it is this one, then confirm the pairing on the phone.
sms.emoji.alt: The pairing emoji is {emoji}. Check that your phone shows the same one, then confirm on the phone.
sms.emoji.waiting: Waiting for you to confirm on your phone…
sms.success: SMS is connected through Google Messages.
sms.migration: This network migrates to the sovereign path on its own when v0.2 ships. Nothing to do now.
sms.failed.google: Google refused the session. The most likely causes are a two-factor challenge you have not answered, cookies copied from a normal window that has since signed out, or Device Bound Session Credentials still switched on. Start again from a private window.
sms.trouble1: Your Android phone must be online for SMS to reach Twalk. If it is off, your carrier queues the messages until it comes back.
sms.trouble2: If Google asks for a two-factor confirmation while you are signing in, answer it before you copy the cookies: a half-finished sign-in produces cookies that do not work.
sms.trouble3: If SMS stops arriving weeks later, Google most likely ended the session. Come back to this screen and paste a fresh set — that is the price of the preview path, and v0.2 removes it.

screen2.recoveryCard.title: About your recovery key
screen2.recoveryCard.body: Your recovery key unlocks your encrypted conversations if you lose this device. It is generated here, in this page, and Twalk never sees it. Write it down or save it in a password manager: you cannot recover it later.

key.title: Save your recovery key
key.intro: This is the only time this key is shown. Nothing on your Twalk server, and nothing at Twalk, can show it to you again.
key.label: Your recovery key
key.copyFailed: Copying failed. Select the key above and copy it by hand.
key.warning.title: What you lose without it
key.warning.body: This key is what unlocks your encrypted conversations on a new device. Without it, and with this device gone, your message history stays encrypted for ever: nobody — not your Twalk server, not Twalk, not your administrator — can read it back or reset it. Your other devices can no longer be verified either, so Twalk would treat them as strangers.
key.warning.noReset: There is no reset in this version. A lost key cannot be replaced; only a new account can.
key.checkbox: I have saved my recovery key in a safe place
key.backup.on: Your key backup is on: new messages are backed up, encrypted with this key.
key.backup.off: Your key backup could not be started. Your recovery key is still valid; open diagnostics before going further.
pdf.title: Twalk recovery key
pdf.intro: This sheet carries the only copy of your Twalk recovery key. It unlocks your encrypted conversations on a new device.
pdf.warning: Keep this sheet. Without this key, and without the device you created it on, your encrypted messages cannot be read back by anyone, and there is no way to reset it.
pdf.advice1: Keep it somewhere you would keep a passport or a bank card: a safe, a locked drawer, a password manager.
pdf.advice2: Do not photograph it, do not email it, and do not put it in a note on your phone.
pdf.advice3: Anyone who has this key can read your conversation history. Twalk never sees it.
pdf.generated: Generated on {date} by the Twalk Companion.

done.body: {id} exists, your cryptographic identity is set up, and your recovery key is saved.
done.next.title: Next: connect a network
done.next.body: Connecting WhatsApp, Signal, SMS or an existing Matrix account is the next step, and it is not built yet. Your account and your key are done.
recover.title: Your keys are not on this device
recover.intro: This is normal, not a failure. Twalk keeps your encryption keys in this browser alone, and a browser can throw them away — iOS deletes them after seven days without opening the app, and clearing your browsing data does it too.
recover.fix: Your recovery key puts them back. Nothing is lost.
recover.install: Install Twalk to your home screen to stop iOS from doing it again.
recover.userId.label: Username
recover.password.label: Password
recover.key.label: Your recovery key
recover.key.not-base58: This key carries a character a recovery key never has. Check for a 0, an O, an I or an l.
recover.key.wrong-length: A recovery key is 12 groups of four characters.
recover.key.not-a-recovery-key: This is a key, but not a Twalk recovery key.
recover.key.parity: There is a typo in this key: two characters do not add up.
recover.error.wrong-recovery-key: This recovery key does not open this account's storage. Check it group by group.
recover.error.no-secret-storage: This account has no recovery storage, so there is nothing a recovery key opens.
recover.error.failed: The recovery could not be completed. {detail}
recover.done.title: This device is back
recover.done.body: Your keys are on this device again and it is verified. Your encrypted conversations open as before.
recover.done.unverified: Your keys came back, but this device could not be verified. Open diagnostics before going further.
recover.done.backup: Your key backup is connected again.
tabs.title: Twalk is open in another tab
tabs.body: Twalk keeps your encryption keys in one place, and two tabs writing to it at once would damage them. Go back to the other tab, or take over here.
persona.assistant.name: Assistant
persona.assistant.description: Your assistant reads the messages arriving on the networks you connected, and suggests replies for you to review. It never sends anything without your approval.
persona.ability.read.label: Read incoming messages
persona.ability.read.detail: On the networks you choose below, and on no others.
persona.ability.read.locked: Always on: an assistant that reads nothing has nothing to suggest.
persona.ability.suggest.label: Suggest replies for your review
persona.ability.suggest.detail: A suggestion waits for you. Nothing leaves your deployment until you approve it.
persona.ability.suggest.locked: Always on: reading and suggesting are one decision in this version — the assistant is active, or it is paused.
persona.title: Activate your first agent
persona.scope.title: What it may read
persona.scope.intro: The assistant is activated on exactly the networks you tick here. Connecting another network later leaves it inactive there until you say otherwise.
persona.scope.matrixHint: Your Twalk deployment keeps no record of the rooms you invited the Sensor into — the access token that did it was forgotten as soon as the invitation was sent. Tick this if you connected your existing Matrix account.
persona.scope.none: No network is connected yet. Connect one first, and the assistant will have something to read.
persona.consent.title: Who the assistant may read, by default
persona.consent.body: Every contact starts at pending. The assistant reads nothing from someone until you decide about them, and there is no rule that grants anyone automatically — this version imports no address book.
persona.removed.title: Two settings the wireframe had, and this screen does not
persona.removed.autoSend: Auto-sending approved replies. It is the one thing in Twalk that would let an agent send without you, so it is not a toggle in an onboarding flow.
persona.removed.hours: Active hours. A time window is a rule to be enforced and audited at runtime; a cosmetic control here would suggest a protection that does not exist.
persona.runtime.title: What happens after you activate it
persona.runtime.body: The decision is recorded and published on your bus, where the agent runtime will read it. That runtime is not deployed yet, so the assistant will produce no suggestions today — activating it now means it starts from the networks you chose, and from nothing else, on the day it runs.
persona.pause.meaning: Pausing an assistant means it receives nothing. It keeps running and stays supervised — it is starved, not stopped.
persona.activated.title: Your assistant is now watching {networks}.
persona.activated.body: It is activated on those networks and on no others.
persona.error.noNetworks: Tick at least one network: an assistant with no perimeter is not a decision the deployment can record.
persona.error.refused: Your deployment refused the decision ({error}). Nothing was recorded.
persona.error.unreachable: Your deployment could not be reached. Nothing was recorded — try again.
